topic: Sound-and-complete lagged micro-effect identification from latent-confounded summary time-series graphs. Fix a finite observed coordinate set, lag bound L, directed/bidirected summary H, X,Y,gamma and x. Quantify over every positive finite-alphabet strictly stationary order-L time-homogeneous semi-Markovian SCM with acyclic instantaneous slices and exact summary H. Construct a terminating graph-native TID-SCG procedure that either outputs one finite-cylinder do-free functional valid for every compatible SCM or a finite lag-switch-hedge certificate constructing two compatible stationary SCMs with the same entire observed process law and unequal P(Y_0|do(X_-gamma=x)). Prove soundness, completeness and an explicit termination bound through a lag-robust intrinsic-district transducer; refinement enumeration, generic QE and tautological model gluing do not qualify. Add cylinder plug-in and HAC delta-method inference under positivity and geometric beta-mixing. Consumer: EasyRCA lag-specific anomaly-transmission ranking under hidden confounding. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: An independent-shift construction preserves whole-process observational equality, intervention separation, lag bounds, positivity and exact summaries when lifting finite collisions; an acyclic directed-summary subclass reduces to one ordinary ID call on at most n(nL+1) ancestral vertices. The repaired XOR witness gives 19/50 versus 31/50, and a separate positive stationary lag-switch pair has identical observed process laws but effects 13/50 versus 1/2. Checks show raw quotienting need not preserve fixability and per-refinement ID is insufficient. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a bounded uniform fixing normal form whose states either compile one universal finite-cylinder arithmetic functional or extract two positive temporal-role SCMs, including disagreement between individually identifiable refinements. EARLY KILL TEST: For |V|<=3 and L=1, test the proposed states and rewrites on the front-door witness, the offset-sensitive fixing counterexample and the stationary lag-switch pair; pivot if the procedure accepts the collision, rejects front-door, conflates offsets or needs unrestricted elimination. open_problems.open_problem: Give a sound-and-complete, graph-native identification procedure for the lag-specific micro total effect P(Y_0 | do(X_{-gamma}=x)) uniformly over all positive stationary bounded-lag semi-Markovian refinements of a directed/bidirected summary graph.

source_refs.claim: The paper treats hidden-confounded micro total effects in summary causal graphs but provides sufficient front-door-type conditions rather than a complete procedure.
source_refs.author: Charles K. Assaad

source_refs.claim: Do-calculus is proved sound and complete for macro total effects in latent-confounded SCGs, while the paper explicitly distinguishes macro from micro queries.
source_refs.author: Simon Ferreira and Charles K. Assaad

source_refs.claim: A bounded segment suffices for causal ID in a fully specified periodic latent-confounded time-series graph; uncertainty over summary-graph refinements is not treated.
source_refs.author: Erik L. Jahn, Karthik Karnik, and Leonard J. Schulman
source_refs.venue: Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning

source_refs.claim: The paper gives a complete characterization only for identification by common adjustment in SCGs under causal sufficiency.
source_refs.author: Clément Yvernes, Emilie Devijver, and Eric Gaussier

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest micro-effect result under hidden confounding is criterion-specific and sufficient, whereas completeness has been obtained only for macro cluster interventions or for a fully specified periodic fine graph. An SCG represents many lag refinements whose offset-specific latent projections can have different districts and fixing orders. A complete procedure therefore needs a finite state representation that preserves temporal offsets and decides whether one observational functional is valid over the entire refinement class, including cases where every refinement is individually identifiable but the resulting functionals disagree.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A terminating algorithm with an explicit size bound that returns either one finite-cylinder do-free arithmetic functional valid for every compatible stationary SCM or a finite lag-switch hedge yielding two positive exact-summary stationary SCMs with the same observed process law and unequal micro effects.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames exactly the micro-versus-summary tension under latent confounding and explains why ordinary adjustment is insufficient.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Experiments are costly -> only a temporally abstract SCG may be available -> hidden confounding defeats adjustment -> seek identification of a lag-specific micro intervention from the abstraction.

method_exemplars.technique: Recursive district decomposition and hedge extraction prove that algorithmic failure supplies a two-model nonidentifiability witness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The temporal procedure needs the same functional-or-certificate duality, but with districts indexed by lag roles and uniformity over refinements.

method_exemplars.technique: Possible-c-component regions and bucket-wise fixing provide a complete identification recursion over a class of compatible causal diagrams.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems demand one functional over a partially specified graph; the temporal transfer must replace fixed PAG buckets by offset-aware refinement states.

method_exemplars.technique: Compile graphical fixing and identification steps into weight-based estimating equations and influence-function estimators with efficiency and robustness results.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the temporal procedure emits a finite-cylinder hidden-variable functional, this is the closest template for turning that output into an estimator and limit theory.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize when all lag refinements of a summary graph induce the same observational functional for a micro effect, including when refinements are separately identifiable but admit no common fixing derivation.

source_refs.claim: The paper separates identification through every graph from identification by one common do-calculus proof and leaves their general relationship conjectural.
source_refs.author: Clément Yvernes, Emilie Devijver, Marianne Clausel, and Eric Gaussier

source_refs.claim: A complete calculus and algorithm decide a common causal functional over every graph represented by a finite PAG.
source_refs.author: Amin Jaber, Adèle H. Ribeiro, Jiji Zhang, and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Intrinsic sets and fixing kernels characterize identifiable effects in a fixed latent-projection ADMG.
source_refs.author: Thomas S. Richardson, Robin J. Evans, James M. Robins, and Ilya Shpitser

open_problems.why_unsolved: The abstraction hierarchy shows that agreement of graph-specific formulas and existence of one uniform do-calculus derivation are logically different notions. PAG completeness resolves class-wide identification on a fixed vertex set, but lag refinements of an SCG change the time-indexed vertices, ancestral margins, and intrinsic districts themselves. The region/fixing recursion must therefore be replaced by temporal-role states capable of comparing algebraic functionals produced along different refinement paths without incorrectly quotienting offset-sensitive fixability.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient offset-sensitive graphical characterization of functional agreement across all compatible lag refinements, together with either a common finite-cylinder functional or a finite pair of identifiable refinements whose induced functionals disagree on one positive observed process law.

writing_exemplar.why: Its hierarchy cleanly motivates why graphwise identifiability, a common proof, and a common functional must not be conflated.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A causal abstraction denotes many diagrams -> several inequivalent notions of identification arise -> graphwise success need not supply a uniform proof -> determine functional agreement for temporal refinements.

method_exemplars.technique: Form regions from possible c-components and recursively remove fixable buckets while preserving completeness over a diagram class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is the temporal analogue of class-wide PAG identification, with lag roles replacing fixed buckets.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent latent-variable equality constraints through kernels obtained by fixing and characterize identification using reachable intrinsic sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Functional comparison across refinements must track which kernels and intrinsic districts survive each offset-sensitive fixing sequence.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate fixing factorizations into estimable weight representations and influence functions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This provides machinery for comparing the statistical implementations of syntactically different graphwise formulas once their functional agreement is established.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine a sharp finite look-back and state-complexity bound for deciding lag-specific micro-effect identification uniformly over all bounded-lag refinements of a latent-confounded summary graph.

source_refs.claim: The paper proves a constant look-back bound for a fully specified periodic latent-confounded graph, depending on graph width and maximum latency.
source_refs.author: Erik L. Jahn, Karthik Karnik, and Leonard J. Schulman
source_refs.venue: Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning

source_refs.claim: Summary graphs omit lag information and represent full-time graphs with potentially different skeletons and orientations; the paper handles causally sufficient effects using adjustment.
source_refs.author: Charles K. Assaad, Emilie Devijver, Eric Gaussier, Gregor Gössler, and Anouar Meynaoui

source_refs.claim: Hidden-confounded micro-effect identification is established only under sufficient front-door-type SCG conditions, without a general uniform horizon theorem.
source_refs.author: Charles K. Assaad

open_problems.why_unsolved: The finite-segment theorem applies after the entire periodic graph, including every edge lag, is known. In an SCG, an obstruction can migrate through time as different abstract edges realize different lags, so it is unknown whether the fully specified look-back bound remains uniform under refinement uncertainty or whether a larger transducer-state bound is necessary. The shift and ancestral-truncation lemma must be strengthened to preserve exact summary realization and all competing offset assignments rather than merely translating one fixed graph.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit computable bound f(n,L,gamma) on the oldest time index and number of transducer states needed by a complete SCG micro-ID procedure, accompanied by a matching or near-matching family of stationary lag-switch instances proving a lower bound.

writing_exemplar.why: It uses the relevant infinite-graph-to-finite-decision motivation arc and states the dependence on graph width and latency.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Time-series causal graphs are infinite -> naïve ID appears to need unbounded history -> periodic bounded-lag structure permits a finite segment -> seek a uniform sharp bound under summary uncertainty.

method_exemplars.technique: Shift nonidentifiability obstructions and truncate to a bounded ancestral segment on which ordinary ID decides the query.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired theorem must strengthen this truncation proof from one periodic graph to every lag refinement represented by an SCG.

method_exemplars.technique: Extract finite hedges from failed district recursion and convert them into observationally indistinguishable causal models.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A lower bound requires finite obstruction families whose necessary hedge depth grows with temporal state complexity.

method_exemplars.technique: Compile a finite identification recursion into estimable weights and influence-function representations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A finite horizon becomes statistically useful when its resulting cylinder functional can be estimated without reopening the infinite graph.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop valid single-trajectory plug-in and HAC inference for arbitrary positive finite-cylinder micro-effect functionals emitted by a latent-confounded summary-graph identification algorithm under geometric beta-mixing.

source_refs.claim: The paper converts hidden-variable graphical identification outputs into influence-function and weight-based estimators in the independent-sample setting.
source_refs.author: Rohit Bhattacharya, Razieh Nabi, and Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: The paper proves asymptotically valid causal testing for stationary beta-mixing processes, but for synthetic-control treatment trajectories rather than graph-identified cylinder functionals.
source_refs.author: Davide Viviano and Jelena Bradic

source_refs.claim: Direct i.i.d. causal estimators can be inconsistent because past dependence creates extra paths; the paper derives specialized estimators for linear instrumental time series.
source_refs.author: Nikolaj Thams, Rikke Søndergaard, Sebastian Weichwald, and Jonas Peters

source_refs.claim: The paper develops hidden-variable identification and estimation with dependent data for segregated and chain graphs, not stationary overlapping cylinder counts from one time series.
source_refs.author: Eli Sherman and Ilya Shpitser

open_problems.why_unsolved: Hidden-variable graphical inference supplies influence-function machinery primarily for i.i.d. samples, while dependent-data work addresses different graph semantics or specialized linear and synthetic-control estimands. For a generic temporal-ID output, the empirical inputs are overlapping cylinder frequencies from one trajectory, so their score vector has a long-run covariance and denominators inherited from fixing kernels. The proof must establish a joint mixing CLT for every required cell, differentiability of the compiled rational functional on a positivity region, consistency of a bandwidth-dependent HAC matrix, and invariance to algebraically equivalent functional representations.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A cylinder-frequency plug-in estimator with an explicit gradient, a root-T Gaussian limit under stated geometric beta-mixing and positivity conditions, a consistent HAC variance estimator, and asymptotically valid confidence intervals for every functional in the procedure's finite output language.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates inference by showing why time dependence invalidates a naïve transfer of i.i.d. causal estimation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A causal effect is identified graphically -> observations come from one dependent trajectory -> naïve i.i.d. estimation mishandles the past -> construct dependence-aware estimation and inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate hidden-variable identifying functionals and derive influence-function and weight representations tied to fixing sequences.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The emitted temporal functional has analogous nested-kernel algebra, but its empirical process is dependent.

method_exemplars.technique: Use sample splitting and block resampling to obtain asymptotic size control under stationary beta-mixing.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a causal single-trajectory dependence argument adaptable to overlapping cylinder statistics.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate long-run covariance using a positive-semidefinite lag-window HAC estimator and prove its consistency under weak dependence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The multivariate cylinder-count CLT produces exactly the long-run covariance object needed by the delta method.

open_problems.open_problem: When a lag-specific micro effect is not point identified from a latent-confounded summary graph, derive graph-native sharp bounds over positive stationary finite-alphabet bounded-lag SCMs without enumerating all lag refinements or invoking unrestricted polynomial elimination.

source_refs.claim: Discrete causal bounding problems for a fixed canonical DAG reduce to polynomial programs that can establish sharpness or epsilon-sharpness.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, and Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: The paper prunes response-function linear programs for hidden-confounded fixed graphs, highlighting exponential growth in generic causal-bound computation.
source_refs.author: Madhumitha Shridharan and Garud Iyengar

source_refs.claim: The closest latent-confounded SCG result provides point-identification conditions but no sharp identified set outside those conditions.
source_refs.author: Charles K. Assaad

open_problems.why_unsolved: Static response-function programs assume one fixed finite causal graph. A summary graph denotes a family of time-indexed refinements, while strict stationarity couples response distributions across shifts and exact-summary constraints require every abstract edge to be realized without introducing others. Directly canonicalizing each refinement neither proves sharpness over the whole process class nor yields a graph-native terminating method. The finite response-type reduction must instead become a bounded temporal-role canonicalization preserving stationarity, exact summaries, and whole-process observational equality.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite graph-derived optimization or symbolic recursion whose lower and upper values equal the infimum and supremum of P(Y_0 | do(X_{-gamma}=x)) over all compatible stationary SCMs, together with finite extremizing lag-switch models and an explicit termination bound.

writing_exemplar.why: It gives a clear motivation from failure of point identification to a mathematically sharp range while emphasizing computational tractability.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Point identification fails under hidden structure -> arbitrary extra assumptions are undesirable -> characterize every compatible causal value -> compute a sharp identified interval.

method_exemplars.technique: Canonicalize finite-alphabet SCMs into generalized response types and express observational constraints and causal targets as polynomial programs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination is also a discrete hidden-variable causal functional, but temporal-role sharing and exact-summary constraints must be incorporated into the canonicalization.

method_exemplars.technique: Prune causal response-function programs using query structure and derive closed forms for special hidden-confounding families.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A viable temporal bound must exploit the local query and lag structure instead of materializing the complete refinement space.

method_exemplars.technique: Propagate empirical uncertainty through estimated sharp-bound programs while maintaining valid outer bounds during incomplete optimization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The temporal analogue would require confidence regions for bound endpoints computed from dependent cylinder frequencies.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a hidden-confounding-robust lag-specific anomaly-transmission ranking for EasyRCA that ranks only universally identified micro effects and certifiably abstains on unresolved lag-switch comparisons.

source_refs.claim: EasyRCA uses an acyclic summary graph and ranks roots partly by comparing direct effects across normal and anomalous regimes, while assuming jointly independent noises.
source_refs.author: Charles K. Assaad, Imad Ez-zejjari, and Lei Zan

source_refs.claim: Selected lag-specific micro total effects can remain identifiable from an SCG despite latent confounding under sufficient front-door-type conditions.
source_refs.author: Charles K. Assaad

source_refs.claim: Complete direct-effect identification and finite adjustment sets are available for linear causally sufficient summary-graph models, not nonlinear hidden-confounded micro effects.
source_refs.author: Simon Ferreira and Charles K. Assaad

open_problems.why_unsolved: EasyRCA's effect-comparison stage relies on causal sufficiency and adjustment-identifiable direct effects. With a bidirected summary graph, the same abstract relation can occur at different lags and can be confounded, so an estimated edge score may represent no refinement-invariant intervention effect. The scanned RCA literature does not propagate identification failures into the ranking: the closest hidden-confounded SCG paper supplies only sufficient micro-effect criteria, while EasyRCA assumes independent noise. The consumer layer must distinguish identified comparisons from unresolved ones and control sampling reversals of identified orderings.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A ranking-and-abstention theorem mapping each candidate anomaly edge to a universally identified lag-specific micro-effect functional or certificate, proving refinement-invariant ordering above a stated effect-gap margin, and giving HAC-based rank consistency from one mixing trajectory.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the destination problem, operational workflow, and direct-effect comparison motivation without implying that hidden confounding is solved.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Collective anomalies propagate through a dynamic system -> a validated summary graph narrows root-cause search -> effect changes rank candidate roots -> hidden confounding requires identification-aware ranking and abstention.

method_exemplars.technique: Lift front-door blocking conditions to temporally abstract SCGs to identify selected micro total effects despite latent confounding.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the closest existing graph-native route from a hidden-confounded SCG to the lag-specific scores required by the ranking.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive weight-based and influence-function estimators for identified hidden-variable effects.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The ranking needs uncertainty estimates for non-adjustment identification formulas before declaring pairwise score comparisons.

method_exemplars.technique: Obtain causal testing guarantees under stationary beta-mixing using block-based inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: EasyRCA observes time-indexed regimes, so rank validity requires dependence-aware comparison rather than i.i.d. standard errors.

literature_map:
1. Shpitser and Pearl (AAAI 2006; JMLR 2008) provide the fixed-ADMG benchmark: recursive ID returns an observational functional or a hedge witnessing nonidentifiability.
2. Richardson, Evans, Robins, and Shpitser (Annals of Statistics 2023) recast hidden-variable identification through fixing kernels and intrinsic sets, the closest machinery for an intrinsic-district transducer.
3. Assaad et al. (UAI 2024, arXiv:2310.14691) identify micro total effects from time-series graph abstractions under causal sufficiency, using adjustment and no latent bidirected structure.
4. Yvernes, Devijver, and Gaussier (UAI 2025) complete the common-adjustment problem for SCGs, but remain criterion-specific and causally sufficient.
5. Assaad (TMLR 2025, arXiv:2406.05805) is the closest target paper: it gives sufficient front-door-type conditions for hidden-confounded micro total effects, not sound-and-complete micro ID.
6. Ferreira and Assaad (AAAI 2025) prove do-calculus soundness and completeness for macro SCG effects and explicitly separate macro from micro queries.
7. Anand, Ribeiro, Tian, and Bareinboim (AAAI 2023, arXiv:2202.12263) prove complete macro identification for cluster DAGs, showing that abstraction-wide ID is possible when clusters are intervention units.
8. Jaber, Ribeiro, Zhang, and Bareinboim (NeurIPS 2022) give complete PAG identification through possible-c-components and regions on a fixed finite vertex set.
9. Yvernes et al. (CAR at UAI 2025, arXiv:2507.06213) distinguish graphwise functional agreement from a single common do-calculus proof and leave their general relationship conjectural.
10. Jahn, Karnik, and Schulman (CLeaR 2025, arXiv:2504.20172) prove that ordinary ID on a bounded segment decides effects in a fully specified periodic latent-confounded time graph; uniform summary-refinement bounds remain absent.
11. Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser (JMLR 2022, arXiv:2003.12659) compile hidden-variable ID into weight and influence-function estimators, but use independent-sample asymptotics.
12. Thams et al. (JMLR 2024, arXiv:2203.06056) show that time-series memory invalidates naïve i.i.d. IV reasoning and derive specialized linear estimators after graph marginalization.
13. Sherman and Shpitser (NeurIPS 2018, arXiv:1902.01443) combine hidden variables and dependent data through segregated graphs, but not stationary SCG refinement classes.
14. Viviano and Bradic (Journal of Econometrics 2023, arXiv:1904.01490) provide causal inference under stationary beta-mixing; Newey and West (Econometrica 1987) provide the HAC covariance template.
15. EasyRCA (Assaad, Ez-zejjari, and Zan, AISTATS 2023, arXiv:2303.04038) compares regime-specific direct effects for anomaly localization but assumes jointly independent noises and thus causal sufficiency.
